Excellent data. Let me analyze what I have:

**NBA (ECF Game 2 — Knicks 105, Cavs 87 with 2:46 left):**
- Knicks: 52% FG, 31 assists, only 6 turnovers — a remarkably clean game
- Cavs: 38% FG, 26.5% from three (9-34) — historically bad 3-point shooting
- James Harden: 5-14 FG, -21 plus/minus — the big number
- Josh Hart: 26 pts, 7 ast, 4 reb, +23 — the story
- Jalen Brunson: 13 assists — brilliant playmaking
- The Knicks outshot them 52% vs 38%, plus the assists disparity (31 vs 15) tells the real story

**NHL (ECF Game 1 — Canadiens 5, Hurricanes 2 with ~8 min left):**
- Frederik Andersen: .762 SV% — catastrophic for a playoff game
- Jakub Dobes (Mtl): .920 SV% on 25 shots
- Carolina dominated shots 25-21 but lost 5-2 — completely fluky shot quality
- Montreal blocked 25 shots vs Carolina's 12 — incredible shot suppression
- CAR had 31 hits vs MTL's 14 — dominated physically but lost badly

The NHL story is remarkable — Carolina being the #1 seed (53-22-7), generating more shots, more hits, winning faceoffs (54.9%), yet getting torched 5-2. The Montreal shot-blocking story (25 blocked shots!) is the angle.
